inspection_summary: Verified the frozen 333343-byte UTF-8 source as SHA-256 79af10f446656c1eb0c970a2ffa58cdb5b7b0b3aa3ccbe4c61209a1164896e7f and 5479 Python str.splitlines() lines, then inspected every line. The article develops a complete chain from critical-line random shifts through shifted two-point estimates and randomized Euler products to generalized-function limits, separates a Gaussian log-correlated core from smooth arithmetic error, derives complex, subcritical-real, and critical chaos, and matches the mesoscopic core with Haar-unitary characteristic polynomials. Formula extraction has control-glyph and conjugation risk, but the prose-supported mechanisms are recoverable; exact displayed notation should be scan-verified before downstream quotation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why the critical-line limit is distribution-valued
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The failure of continuous functional limits is resolved not by hiding roughness but by identifying a randomized Euler-product boundary distribution whose radial blow-up precludes even a local measure representation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis concerns the randomized/global statistical limit and does not settle microscopic zeta behavior.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The Hilbert-transform rescue of dependent complex chaos
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The special real-imaginary dependence generates a Cauchy or Hilbert-transform singularity; analytic one-sided spectral structure turns the apparently nonintegrable two-point function into an L2-bounded generalized-function martingale.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The argument is specific to this covariance and analytic boundary structure, not a universality theorem for arbitrary complex chaos.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic is compressed into a smooth factor
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After the first prime harmonic is coupled to a log-correlated Gaussian field, higher prime powers, prime-location irregularity, phase freezing, and coupling errors all converge smoothly, so the singular universal component separates from an arithmetic smooth multiplier.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The decomposition is proved for the randomized Euler-product model; transfer to actual zeta uses the separate global-limit theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Nested approximation triangle from zeta shifts to randomized Euler products
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fourier-sampled test norms and uniform two-point asymptotics control truncation, prime-phase equidistribution identifies each finite randomized product, and Hilbert-valued martingale convergence closes the function-space limit in a fixed order.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The method establishes existence and convergence under the stated Sobolev regularization, not sharp rates or optimal test spaces.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Mesoscopic zero-mode separation and projective universality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Dilation separates an exploding scalar Gaussian mode from a delta-independent strict log chaos; quotienting generalized functions by nonzero scalars makes zeta and CUE converge to the same mesoscopic spatial law.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only sufficiently slow deterministic shrinking scales are constructed, and equality is modulo scalar factors rather than pointwise equality.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Real-chaos phase transition transferred through the smooth error
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once prime covariance is identified as one-half logarithmic plus smooth, subcritical uniform integrability and critical covariance comparison transfer Gaussian-chaos phase behavior to normalized absolute powers of randomized zeta.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: For actual zeta shifts the analogous measures remain conjectural because the required moment and correlation asymptotics are unavailable.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Moment asymptotics are the bridge still missing for actual zeta chaos
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper can prove the second shifted moment needed for generalized-function convergence, but real and imaginary chaos for actual zeta would demand substantially stronger absolute and multipoint correlations, with zeros adding an extra obstruction for the imaginary part.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: A proof-search failure or missing estimate would not refute the conjectured chaos picture; it identifies the present analytic bottleneck.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Random-matrix transfer uses different exact inputs but the same approximation architecture
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Toeplitz determinant asymptotics replace zeta divisor-sum estimates, Gaussian trace limits replace prime-phase equidistribution, and dilation plus Brownian coupling then recover the same mesoscopic chaos component.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The global inputs are model-specific and the paper does not claim that all microscopic statistics coincide.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two routes to the global limit trade quantitative control for simpler evidence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Euler-product truncation gives the strongest variance and function-space control through explicit two-point kernels, whereas finite Dirichlet polynomials bypass the hardest mixed estimate but provide weaker quantitative approximation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These are alternative proofs of the same randomized limit, not independent validation of the limiting law.
